Q: Merging files, but with a twist A:

At the moment, I don't see any actual bash answers, so I'll just add this for posterity, following your original algorithm. (Note: imho, don't worry about Big-O unless your data is relatively large, but this seems like metadata and not big-data, therefore do whatever is easiest first, and if that's too slow, at least you'll have a script to regression test against for the next, optimized version.)

$ cat good.txt | while read line; do  printf "${line},"; grep "^${line%%-*}" dirs.txt | paste -sd ' ' - ; done | sort -u
b01-1-ws001,b01-1
b01-ws001,b01-1
b07-1-control,b07 b07-1 b07-2
b07-1-ws001,b07 b07-1 b07-2
b07-1-ws002,b07 b07-1 b07-2
b07-1-ws004,b07 b07-1 b07-2
b07-1-ws006,b07 b07-1 b07-2
b07-1-ws007,b07 b07-1 b07-2
b07-1-ws099,b07 b07-1 b07-2
b07-2-control,b07 b07-1 b07-2

Fyi, I just added the optional ending sort -u to remove duplicate lines, should there be any. It's not efficient, like I said, except for it's fast to code up, and honestly, isn't that the most important type of efficiency? :-)

Notes:

  • the first printf intentionally omits a newline, the paste strips out all newlines from the grep output, replacing with spaces, except for the last one
  • bash parameter expansion ${variable%%pattern} removes the longest matching pattern from the end of the variable, so everything after the first dash "-"

Q: Looking for a term of art ("pseudo-phantom type"?) in typeful programming A:

One way to describe this is as a zero-multiplicity. Haskell's Linear types currently do not support that, but they were designed with such extensions in mind.

Idris, a language with quantitative types, does support a zero multiplicity:

https://idris2.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorial/multiplicities.html

Q: How to enlarge the Netbeans IDE icon, menu and toolbar fonts? A:

If Netbeans is running, shut down Netbeans.

1. Make sure you have an icon in your System Tray for Netbeans.

2. Right click on the Netbeans icon in the system tray (usually at bottom of home desktop screen) to get a popup menu

3. Right click on the “Netbeans 8.2” option in that popup menu to get to Properties

4. Click on “Properties”

5. Within Properties, edit the “Target:” field to be something like the following:

"C:\Program Files\NetBeans 8.2\bin\netbeans64.exe" --fontsize 60

6. Click “Apply” and “OK”

7. Start up Netbeans by clicking the Netbeans icon in the System Tray.

Q: How to reuse one things everywhere? A:

"we need to use interface to reuse again and again" => no, we don't. Why do you think that?
Re-using is simply you creating a class or a method, and using it on multiple places in your code, instead of duplicating the code where you want to use it.

Q: SQL recursive CTE exit and return item where a descending table and a ascending formula meet A:

The code below makes a couple of changes to your code.

First, you need to enumerate the source data, so that you can process one row at a time. I used ROW_NUMBER for that.

Second, the recursive branch's WHERE clause should return TRUE when you want it to carry on iterating, not when you want it to stop.

Finally, you need to pick just the last row from the CTE.

WITH RECURSIVE 
  enumerated (
    id,
    c
  )
AS
(
  SELECT
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY c DESC)   id,
    c
  FROM
    pc
),
  meet_in_middle (
    c_id,
    c_val, 
    iterated_calc
  )
AS
(
  -- Anchor dataset with a dummy row, in case `pc` is empty, 
  -- and the first iterative calculation value
  VALUES (0, 0, 0)

  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT
    -- next row of `pc`
    next.*,
    -- next calculated value
    prev.iterated_calc + 1 
  FROM
    meet_in_middle   AS prev
  INNER JOIN
    enumerated       AS next
      ON next.id = prev.c_id + 1
      -- The id of the next `pc` row
      -- Similarity to iteratively calculated value is coincidental
  WHERE
    prev.iterated_calc <= next.c
    -- Only iterate if the previous iterated calculation
    -- does NOT satisfy our condition
)
SELECT
  iterated_calc
FROM
  meet_in_middle
ORDER BY
  c_id DESC
LIMIT
  1
-- Get only the last row from the CTE
;
iterated_calc
3

fiddle

Note: this abuses recursive CTEs to replicate a linear loop. As such it is highly inefficient and is really only valid to demonstrate how recursive CTEs work. In most cases, reframing as a set based approach will be much preferred.
